note: Declarative definitions for Article 22. Not Cloud Monitoring API payloads; this module creates no cloud resources.

metrics.name: money.http.responses
metrics.description: HTTP responses by class. The signal that stays green in scenario S04.

metrics.name: money.provider.attempts
metrics.description: Calls made to the external provider, by what the provider said.

metrics.name: money.events.delivered
metrics.description: Event deliveries into the ledger poster, by what the consumer did with them.

metrics.name: money.effects.applied
metrics.description: Externally visible money-moving effects actually applied.

metrics.name: money.state.oldest_age_seconds
metrics.description: Age of the oldest operation in each non-terminal state.

metrics.name: money.state.count
metrics.description: Operations in each non-terminal state. Healthy on its own in S03.

metrics.name: money.ledger.imbalance_minor
metrics.description: Absolute difference between debits and credits, in minor units.

metrics.name: money.invariant.violations
metrics.description: Open violations per business invariant. The red light in a green dashboard.

metrics.name: money.reconciliation.oldest_age_seconds
metrics.description: Age of the oldest open exception by kind. Moves when the count does not.

metrics.name: money.settlement.lateness_seconds
metrics.description: How long the oldest captured effect has waited for settlement evidence.

metrics.name: money.checker.staleness_seconds
metrics.description: Time since each periodic checker last completed. Absence of signal is not health.

invariants.title: the journal balances
invariants.statement: For every live posting group, the sum of debits equals the sum of credits.
invariants.invisibleTo: request success rate, latency, error rate — the posting request returns 200

invariants.title: the posting equals the effect
invariants.statement: For every provider effect with a posting group, the amount credited to the customer equals the amount the provider captured.
invariants.invisibleTo: provider success rate — the capture succeeded and the posting succeeded

invariants.title: no posting without an effect
invariants.statement: Every posting group references a provider effect that exists.
invariants.invisibleTo: event delivery metrics — the event was delivered and acknowledged

invariants.title: one effect per operation
invariants.statement: A logical operation causes at most one externally visible money-moving effect.
invariants.invisibleTo: arrival counts — every arrival was handled successfully

invariants.title: the customer is told the truth
invariants.statement: No operation reports SUCCEEDED to the customer without a captured provider effect, and none reports FAILED when one exists.
invariants.invisibleTo: the status endpoint's own availability and latency

invariants.title: nothing is stuck
invariants.statement: No operation remains in a non-terminal state for longer than its state-age budget.
invariants.invisibleTo: queue depth and in-flight counts, which stay small while an age grows

invariants.title: settlement arrives
invariants.statement: Every captured effect older than the settlement budget appears in settlement evidence.
invariants.invisibleTo: every online signal; nothing in the request path knows settlement is late

invariants.title: the exception queue drains
invariants.statement: Open reconciliation exceptions stay within budget in both count and age.
invariants.invisibleTo: throughput, which rises while the residue accumulates

slos.title: checkout accepts a payment
slos.specification: The proportion of checkout requests that receive a non-5xx response.
slos.note: This is the number a dashboard shows first and the one that stays green in S04.

slos.title: checkout responds quickly
slos.specification: The proportion of checkout requests served faster than 400 ms.
slos.implementation: money.http.latency{service=checkout-api}, p95 against a 400 ms threshold.
slos.note: Fast is not the same as correct, and this objective knows nothing about the ledger.

slos.title: the status a customer sees is true
slos.specification: INV-5 holds: nobody is told SUCCEEDED without a provider effect, or FAILED when one exists.
slos.implementation: money.invariant.violations{invariant=INV-5}, evaluated out of band against durable state.
slos.note: The status endpoint can be fast, available and lying. Its own SLIs cannot tell.

slos.title: an accepted payment reaches a terminal state
slos.specification: The proportion of operations that leave every non-terminal state within the state-age budget (INV-6).
slos.implementation: money.state.oldest_age_seconds per state, against the budget.
slos.note: Age, not count. A small count with a growing age is the stuck case.

slos.title: unknown outcomes are resolved
slos.specification: The proportion of provider calls whose outcome is known within 10 minutes, with INV-4 holding throughout.
slos.note: An unknown outcome is a state to resolve, not an error to retry blindly.

slos.title: the journal balances
slos.specification: INV-1 holds. There is no acceptable rate of unbalanced journals.
slos.note: Expressed as time to detect and time to repair rather than as a ratio. See ADR-001.

slos.title: postings match effects
slos.specification: INV-2 and INV-3 hold for every live posting group.
slos.note: A posting that succeeded and a posting that is right are different claims.

slos.title: settlement evidence arrives
slos.specification: INV-7 holds: every capture older than 48 hours has settlement evidence.
slos.note: Nothing in the request path knows this is late. Only a periodic check does.

slos.title: the exception queue drains
slos.specification: INV-8 holds in both count and age.
slos.note: Throughput rises while the residue accumulates, so throughput is the wrong signal.

alerts.title: checkout availability below objective
alerts.condition: SLO-C1 is below 99.9% over the alerting window

alerts.title: provider outcome unknown beyond budget
alerts.asks: Did money move for an operation we have given up on?

alerts.title: journal does not balance
alerts.asks: Which journal, which operation, how much, and since when?

alerts.title: posting does not match the provider effect
alerts.asks: Does what we recorded match what the provider did?

alerts.title: posting references an effect nobody recorded
alerts.asks: Did we book money that no provider effect accounts for?

alerts.title: one operation produced more than one effect
alerts.asks: Has a customer been charged twice?

alerts.title: customer status contradicts durable state
alerts.asks: Have we told somebody something untrue?

alerts.title: operation stuck in a non-terminal state
alerts.asks: Which operation stopped moving, and at which step?

alerts.title: capture without settlement evidence
alerts.asks: Is the bank short of money we believe we have?

alerts.title: reconciliation exceptions outside budget
alerts.asks: Is the exception queue draining or accumulating?

alerts.title: an invariant checker has stopped reporting
alerts.condition: money.checker.staleness_seconds exceeds the staleness budget for any checker
alerts.asks: Is the dashboard green because the system is healthy or because nothing is looking?

alerts.title: synthetic money-movement canary failed
alerts.condition: money.canary.outcome{result=fail} increased in the last window
alerts.asks: Does a known-good payment still produce the known-good effect?

alerts.title: metric writes refused by the cardinality guard
alerts.condition: the registry refused one or more label writes in the last window
alerts.asks: Which service tried to put an identifier on a metric label?

dashboards.name: money-movement-technical
dashboards.answers: Is the software up, fast, and returning successes?

tiles.title: Response classes by service
tiles.reads: A rising 5xx line is a service problem. A flat zero proves nothing about money.

tiles.title: Request latency p95
tiles.reads: Tail latency by service. Distribution, not mean: a mean hides the tail.

tiles.title: Provider attempts by outcome
tiles.reads: The 'unknown' series is the one to watch; it is not an error, it is an open question.

tiles.title: Event deliveries
tiles.reads: Duplicates suppressed is a health signal, not a defect count.

dashboards.name: money-movement-invariants
dashboards.purpose: Whether the money is where the books say it is.
dashboards.answers: Is anything financially wrong right now, and for how long has it been wrong?

tiles.title: Open invariant violations
tiles.reads: Any non-zero value is an incident. There is no acceptable rate.

tiles.title: Effects applied
tiles.reads: Money-moving effects, not arrivals. Compare with request counts, never substitute them.

tiles.title: Ledger imbalance
tiles.reads: Minor units of difference between debits and credits. The headline of S04.

tiles.title: Oldest operation by state
tiles.reads: Age, beside count. A small count with a growing age is the stuck case.

tiles.title: Operations by state
tiles.reads: Present only so that it can be compared with the tile above it.

tiles.title: Settlement lateness
tiles.reads: How long the oldest capture has waited for bank evidence.

tiles.title: Reconciliation exceptions open
tiles.reads: The count. Read it beside the age tile below, never instead of it.

tiles.title: Reconciliation exceptions: oldest open
tiles.reads: The age series moves first when the queue stops draining.

tiles.title: Checker staleness
tiles.reads: If this grows, every tile above it is unreliable and must be read as unknown.

tiles.title: Canary outcome
tiles.reads: A known-good payment, end to end, on a schedule. A failure here precedes customer reports.
